question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Ahuja is a cleverest lawyer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. clever.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The article "a" cannot be used with the superlative degree ("cleverest"). A superlative always takes "the" (the cleverest). Since the sentence uses "a", the adjective must be in the positive degree — "clever".

◦ Correct: Ahuja is a clever lawyer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "most clever" and Option 3 "cleverer" would also need a comparison ("the most clever", "cleverer than ..."), which is absent here.

• Option 4 "more clever" (comparative) requires "than" — no comparison exists in the sentence.

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: clever – cleverer (with "than") – cleverest (with "the"). Rule: a/an + positive degree, the + superlative degree, comparative + than.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Curse
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Praise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Curse" means to use offensive words against someone; to wish evil or misfortune upon someone. (शाप देना / कोसना)

• Its antonym is "praise", which means to express approval or admiration of someone. (प्रशंसा करना)

◦ Example: Instead of cursing his rival, he began to praise his hard work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Criticise" (to point out faults) and Option 2 "Abuse" (to insult) are synonyms of curse, not antonyms.

• Option 4 "Comment" (to give an opinion) is neutral and unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of curse: abuse, damn, condemn, revile. Antonyms: praise, bless, commend, applaud.

question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank.

She always wears dresses of _________ fashion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. the latest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The latest" means the most recent/newest. Dresses "of the latest fashion" = dresses of the newest style. The superlative "latest" must take the definite article "the". (नवीनतम)

◦ Correct: She always wears dresses of the latest fashion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "late" means delayed/dead (the late Mr Sharma) — it does not mean "newest" here.

• Option 2 "the latter" means the second of two things mentioned — no such pair exists.

• Option 3 "latest" without "the" is incomplete, as a superlative needs the article "the".

NOTE

• Distinguish: later/latest refer to time (the latest news), while latter/last refer to position/order (the latter half, the last chapter).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The discussion led by the scientist was very ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. informative.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the intensifier "very", we use the positive degree of an adjective. "Informative" (giving useful information) fits perfectly. (ज्ञानवर्धक / जानकारीपूर्ण)

◦ Correct: The discussion led by the scientist was very informative.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "more informative" (comparative) needs "than"; Option 4 "most informative" (superlative) needs "the" and a group for comparison — "very" cannot precede either.

• Option 3 "information" is a noun; an adjective is required after "was very".

NOTE

• "Very + positive adjective" (very informative), "much + comparative" (much more informative), "by far + superlative" (by far the most informative).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Manisha had a great feeling for those who were junior than her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. junior to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Latin-origin comparative adjectives such as "junior, senior, superior, inferior, prior, anterior, posterior" take the preposition "to", NOT "than". So "junior to her" is correct.

◦ Correct: Manisha had a great feeling for those who were junior to her.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "junior of" and 3 "junior from" use wrong prepositions.

• Option 4 is wrong because "junior than" is grammatically incorrect and needs substitution.

NOTE

• Remember for SSC exams: senior to, junior to, superior to, inferior to, preferable to, prior to — never "than" with these words.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Wolves’ teeth are larger and strong than dog’s teeth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. stronger.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" demands the comparative degree, and the adjective must stay parallel with "larger". Hence "larger and stronger than". (तुलनात्मक डिग्री)

◦ Correct: Wolves' teeth are larger and stronger than dog's teeth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "more strong" is unidiomatic — short adjectives form the comparative with "-er" (strong → stronger).

• Option 3 "the stronger" wrongly adds the article; Option 4 "strongest" is a superlative and cannot be used with "than".

NOTE

• Parallelism rule: adjectives joined by "and" must be in the same degree — "larger and stronger", "bigger and better". One-syllable adjectives take "-er/-est", not "more/most".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'Native' from the given sentence.

Mr. Smith believes that various tribes are the indigenous habitants of various corners of the world; unlike his contemporaries who have a viewpoint regarding an alien or foreign invasion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Indigenous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Native" means belonging naturally to a place; originating in a particular region. Its closest synonym in the sentence is "indigenous" — occurring/living naturally in a region. (देशज / स्थानीय / मूल निवासी)

◦ Example: Tribes are the native/indigenous inhabitants of these regions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Foreign" (from another country) and Option 3 "Alien" (belonging to another place) are antonyms of native.

• Option 4 "Invasion" (an attack/entry by force) is a noun and unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of native: indigenous, aboriginal, local, domestic. Antonyms: foreign, alien, exotic, immigrant.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Anticipate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Predict.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Anticipate" means to expect or foresee something before it happens. Its closest synonym is "predict" — to say what will happen in the future. (पूर्वानुमान करना / पहले से अपेक्षा करना)

◦ Example: The weather office anticipated/predicted heavy rain over the weekend.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Accuse" (to blame someone), Option 3 "doubt" (to be uncertain) and Option 4 "Conceal" (to hide) are unrelated to expecting something in advance.

NOTE

• Synonyms of anticipate: predict, expect, foresee, forecast, envisage. Antonym: doubt (in the sense of not expecting), be unaware of.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

A few students have condemned the latest project of preparing teaching aids as a waste of money.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Applauded.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Condemned" means expressed strong disapproval of; criticised severely. (निंदा की)

• Its antonym is "applauded" — praised or expressed approval (literally, clapped for). (सराहा / प्रशंसा की)

◦ Example: While a few students condemned the project, the teachers applauded it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Contradicted" (denied/opposed a statement) is closer to a synonym of disapproval.

• Option 2 "Doomed" (destined to fail) and Option 4 "Consolidated" (strengthened/combined) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of condemn: denounce, censure, criticise, deplore. Antonyms: applaud, praise, commend, approve.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Crocodile tears
option_2: To not behave in a fair way
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. An insincere display of grief.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "crocodile tears" means a false, insincere or hypocritical show of sorrow. (घड़ियाली आँसू — दिखावटी दुख)

◦ Example: She shed crocodile tears at the meeting, though she was secretly happy about her rival's failure.

• The idiom comes from the ancient belief that crocodiles weep while devouring their prey.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "An irrevocable step" matches "to cross the Rubicon".

• Option 2 "To not behave in a fair way" matches "to play foul / hit below the belt".

• Option 3 "To please everyone" matches "to run with the hare and hunt with the hounds".

NOTE

• Related idioms: "wear one's heart on one's sleeve" (show feelings openly), "put on an act" (pretend). "Crocodile tears" is a favourite SSC idiom — remember: fake sorrow.

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The magician performed a magnificant trick.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. magnificent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "magnificent", meaning extremely beautiful, grand or impressive. (भव्य / शानदार)

◦ Correct: The magician performed a magnificent trick.

• Spelling key: MAG + NI + FI + CENT (only one "i" before "-cent", no "a").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "magnificant", "magneficent", "magnificante" and "magnificient" are all misspellings — errors occur in the vowels ("a/e/i") before "-cent".

NOTE

• Similar "-cent" spellings often tested in SSC: magnificent, munificent (very generous), beneficent (doing good), reminiscent (reminding of). Related forms: magnificence (noun), magnificently (adverb).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Michael Jackson is known as the King of Pop. He ________ his own genre of music, Pop. His music is spreading its influence and popularity ________ the world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. dominates; around.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dominates" means has a commanding position over; is the most important in. Michael Jackson dominates his own genre, Pop. The singular subject "He" needs the singular verb "dominates". (प्रभुत्व रखता है)

• "Around the world" is the correct fixed expression meaning all over the world. (दुनिया भर में)

◦ Correct: He dominates his own genre of music ... popularity around the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "command" does not agree with "He" (it should be "commands"), and "besides" (in addition to) is wrong.

• Option 3 "beside" means "next to" — incorrect here.

• Option 4 "presides" needs "over" (presides over), and "round the world" is less appropriate in this context.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: singular subject → verb + s/es. Fixed phrases: "around the world", "all over the world", "across the globe".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A blue-eyed boy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. one who is favourite.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a blue-eyed boy" means a person who is someone's favourite; one who is highly favoured and given special treatment (especially by a person in authority). (चहेता / कृपापात्र व्यक्ति)

◦ Example: Rohan is the blue-eyed boy of the manager, so he gets all the important projects.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "an unperceived observer" matches "a fly on the wall".

• Option 2 "a miser" matches "a penny-pincher".

• Option 3 "an unwelcome intruder" matches "a gatecrasher".

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "the apple of one's eye" (someone very dear), "teacher's pet" (a teacher's favourite student). In American English, the phrase is "fair-haired boy".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'Ceased' to fill in the blank.

He was _______ from his job because of his misconduct.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. terminated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ceased" means stopped; brought to an end. Its synonym "terminated" means ended/dismissed. "He was terminated from his job" = his job was brought to an end (he was dismissed). (समाप्त किया गया / नौकरी से हटाया गया)

◦ Correct: He was terminated from his job because of his misconduct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "continued" (kept going) and Option 4 "progressed" (moved forward) are antonyms of ceased.

• Option 3 "commenced" means began — also opposite in sense.

NOTE

• Synonyms of cease/terminate: stop, end, discontinue, halt, conclude. Antonyms: commence, begin, continue, start.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to complete the given sentence in the present perfect continuous tense.

The company ___________________ working towards achievements in curbing slackness and fostering development.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. has been.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The present perfect continuous tense = has/have + been + verb-ing. "The company" is a singular subject, so it takes "has been working". (पूर्ण वर्तमान सतत काल)

◦ Correct: The company has been working towards achievements in curbing slackness and fostering development.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "have been" is used with plural subjects (They have been working).

• Options 2 "are being" and 3 "is being" form the present continuous passive, not the present perfect continuous.

NOTE

• Tense structures for SSC: Present perfect continuous — has/have been + V-ing (since/for); Past perfect continuous — had been + V-ing. Collective nouns like "company", "team", "committee" normally take a singular verb.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The sharpshooter _________ dead a man-eating tiger after it allegedly killed nine people in the last few days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. shot.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct collocation is "shot dead" — to kill by firing a gun. A sharpshooter (an expert marksman) shot dead the man-eating tiger. (गोली मारकर मार डाला)

◦ Correct: The sharpshooter shot dead a man-eating tiger ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fixed dead" and Option 2 "threw dead" are not valid English collocations.

• Option 4 "killed dead" is redundant — "killed" already means caused death.

NOTE

• "Shoot – shot – shot" (V1–V2–V3). Common collocations: "shot dead", "shot at", "gunned down". The word "sharpshooter" itself hints at shooting.

question:
Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error in the given sentence.

The reorganisation of daily life wrought by industrialisation had effects that weakened the material basis for the instietutions of the family and the community.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. institutions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "institutions" — established organisations, customs or systems in a society (here, the family and the community as social institutions). (संस्थाएँ)

◦ Correct: ... weakened the material basis for the institutions of the family and the community.

• Spelling key: IN + STI + TU + TIONS.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "instietutions" (given in the sentence), "instetusion", "instetuitions" and "instetutions" are all misspellings — the correct form has "insti-", not "inste-", and no extra "i".

NOTE

• Related words: institute (verb/noun), institution (noun), institutional (adjective). Do not confuse with "intuition" (instinctive understanding).

question:
The following sentence has been split into segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

He missed the college bus / because he woke up / unpardonably lately in the morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. unpardonably lately in the morning.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is in the word "lately". "Lately" means recently/of late — it does NOT mean "not on time". The correct adverb here is "late" (after the proper time). So the segment should be "unpardonably late in the morning".

◦ Correct: He missed the college bus because he woke up unpardonably late in the morning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "He missed the college bus" and "because he woke up" are grammatically correct segments.

NOTE

• Confusing adverb pairs for SSC: late (after the due time — He came late) vs lately (recently — He has been ill lately); hard (with effort) vs hardly (scarcely); near (close) vs nearly (almost).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the highlighted word(s) in the given sentence.

The sceneries in Darjeeling are breathtaking.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. scenery in Darjeeling is.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Scenery" is an uncountable noun — it has no plural form ("sceneries" is incorrect) and takes a singular verb. Hence "The scenery in Darjeeling is breathtaking".

◦ Correct: The scenery in Darjeeling is breathtaking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 2 and 3 retain the incorrect plural "sceneries".

• Option 1 uses "scenery" correctly but pairs it with the plural past verb "were", which is wrong for a singular uncountable noun in a present-tense statement.

NOTE

• Uncountable nouns that never take "-s" and always take a singular verb: scenery, furniture, information, advice, luggage, machinery, poetry, news. To count them, use "a piece of scenery/furniture/information".

question:
One of the four words in bold in the given sentence is incorrectly spelt. Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

The detectives uncovered a conspirasy to overthrow the government.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. conspirasy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Conspirasy" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "conspiracy" — a secret plan by a group to do something unlawful or harmful. (षड्यंत्र / साज़िश)

◦ Correct: The detectives uncovered a conspiracy to overthrow the government.

• Spelling key: CON + SPI + RA + CY (ends in "-cy", not "-sy").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "detectives" (investigators), "uncovered" (discovered/exposed) and "overthrow" (to remove from power by force) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: conspire (verb), conspirator (person), conspiratorial (adjective). Words ending in "-cy": conspiracy, democracy, accuracy, legacy, fallacy.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Worldwide illiteracy rates have (1)_________ declined in the last few decades. One of the major reasons for this decline is the sharp increase in literacy rates (2)_________ young women, which is a result of specific (3)_________ designed to increase educational opportunities for girls. (4)_________, there are still an estimated 771 million illiterate adults in the world, about two-thirds of whom are (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. consistently.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Consistently" means steadily; in the same way over a period of time without change. Illiteracy rates have "consistently declined in the last few decades" — i.e., they have fallen steadily and continuously. (लगातार / निरंतर)

◦ Correct: Worldwide illiteracy rates have consistently declined in the last few decades.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "thirdly" (in the third place) needs a list of points — none exists here.

• Option 2 "wearily" (tiredly) is illogical for statistics.

• Option 3 "consequently" (as a result) shows a result, but no cause has been stated yet — the decline is being described, not caused.

NOTE

• "Consistently" (steadily, uniformly) vs "constantly" (all the time) vs "consequently" (therefore). Adverbs of manner like "consistently" typically sit between the auxiliary and the main verb: have consistently declined.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Worldwide illiteracy rates have (1)_________ declined in the last few decades. One of the major reasons for this decline is the sharp increase in literacy rates (2)_________ young women, which is a result of specific (3)_________ designed to increase educational opportunities for girls. (4)_________, there are still an estimated 771 million illiterate adults in the world, about two-thirds of whom are (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. among.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Among" is used for more than two people or a group considered collectively. "Literacy rates among young women" = literacy rates within the group of young women. (के बीच — समूह के लिए)

◦ Correct: ... the sharp increase in literacy rates among young women ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "between" is used for two persons/things (between two friends), not for a large group.

• Option 2 "over" (above) and Option 4 "against" (in opposition to) do not fit the sense of "within a group".

NOTE

• Preposition rule for SSC: "between" = two; "among" = more than two/a group. E.g., "Divide the sweets between the two boys but among the five girls".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Worldwide illiteracy rates have (1)_________ declined in the last few decades. One of the major reasons for this decline is the sharp increase in literacy rates (2)_________ young women, which is a result of specific (3)_________ designed to increase educational opportunities for girls. (4)_________, there are still an estimated 771 million illiterate adults in the world, about two-thirds of whom are (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. campaigns.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Campaigns" means organised courses of action/planned activities intended to achieve a particular goal (here, increasing educational opportunities for girls). (अभियान)

◦ Correct: ... which is a result of specific campaigns designed to increase educational opportunities for girls.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "companions" (friends/associates), Option 3 "camisole" (a woman's undergarment) and Option 4 "champions" (winners/supporters) make no sense with "designed to increase educational opportunities".

NOTE

• "Campaign" collocates with: launch/run/lead a campaign, awareness campaign, literacy campaign, election campaign. In India, "Beti Bachao Beti Padhao" is a well-known campaign for girls' education.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Worldwide illiteracy rates have (1)_________ declined in the last few decades. One of the major reasons for this decline is the sharp increase in literacy rates (2)_________ young women, which is a result of specific (3)_________ designed to increase educational opportunities for girls. (4)_________, there are still an estimated 771 million illiterate adults in the world, about two-thirds of whom are (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. However.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "However" shows contrast between two statements. The passage first says illiteracy has declined; then, in contrast, "However, there are still an estimated 771 million illiterate adults". (फिर भी / तथापि)

◦ Correct: However, there are still an estimated 771 million illiterate adults in the world ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Whenever" (at any time when) introduces a time clause — no time reference exists.

• Option 2 "Otherwise" (if not/or else) shows a condition — not intended here.

• Option 3 "Thus" (therefore) shows a result, but the sentence contradicts, not follows from, the earlier one.

NOTE

• Contrast connectors: however, nevertheless, nonetheless, yet, still, on the other hand. They are usually followed by a comma at the start of a sentence.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Worldwide illiteracy rates have (1)_________ declined in the last few decades. One of the major reasons for this decline is the sharp increase in literacy rates (2)_________ young women, which is a result of specific (3)_________ designed to increase educational opportunities for girls. (4)_________, there are still an estimated 771 million illiterate adults in the world, about two-thirds of whom are (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. women.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "about two-thirds of whom" refers to 771 million illiterate adults — a plural group — so the plural noun "women" is required. The passage is about literacy among young women, so the contrast is that most illiterate adults are still women. (महिलाएँ)

◦ Correct: ... about two-thirds of whom are women.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "man" and 2 "woman" are singular and cannot follow the plural verb "are" for two-thirds of 771 million adults.

• Option 3 "child" is singular and also illogical — the passage talks about illiterate adults.

NOTE

• Irregular plurals: man → men, woman → women, child → children. As per UNESCO data, nearly two-thirds of the world's illiterate adults are women — a common fact in SSC comprehension passages.
